chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked him about a man who had children, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. How should we deal with the inheritance of the missing one from his father? He said: 'Keep it aside until he comes.' I said: 'The man is lost and will not be coming.' So he said: 'If the inheritors of the man were reliable with his wealth, distribute it between them, so when he comes, they can return it to him.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for the inheritance of a missing heir whose parent has died?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of provisional inheritance distribution, where the missing heir's share is withheld until his return or declared death, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the rights of the absent party. The condition that remaining heirs must be 'trustworthy' (milā’ bi-mālihi) ensures that the set-aside portion is not misappropriated, highlighting the practical application of amanah in estate management. This ruling balances the need for estate liquidity with the certainty of eventual restitution, a key concept in Usul al-Fiqh regarding gha'ib.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man for whom were children. So one of the children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. How should we deal with the inheritance of the disappeared one from his father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Keep it aside until he comes’. I said, ‘The man is lost and will not be coming’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the inheritors of the man were reliable with his wealth, distribute it between them, so when he comes, they can return it to him’.

A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash ‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who had several sons, of whom one disappeared and he did not know where he was. The man died. What must be done with the share of the legacy for the son who has disappeared? He (the Imam) said, ‘It must be kept aside until he comes? I then said, ‘The man is lost (the father died) he did not come? He (the Imam) said, ‘If the heirs are trusted for his asset, they can distribute among themselves; and when he comes then give it to him?”
A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Hammad from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu Ibrahim ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.
